newsitem.title: USA: UAL posts record first quarter income.
newsitem.headline: UAL posts record first quarter income.

text.p: UAL Corp. earned a record $105 million in the first quarter as strong demand for domestic air travel fuelled a sharp turnaround from a year-earlier loss, the parent of United Airlines said Tuesday.
UAL said its income meant earnings of 92 cents a share and came on revenue of $4.12 billion. A year earlier, UAL lost $23 million, or 90 cents a share, on sales of $3.74 billion.
Northwest Airlines Corp. also reported a strong quarter, posting income of $64.6 million, up 21 percent from the first quarter of 1996, and sales of $2.38 billion, an increase of 5 percent.
Northwest warned, however, that it expected the second quarter to be more challenging as a result of high fuel costs and a weak Japanese yen.
Its stock fell 12.5 cents to $38.125 on the Nasdaq market.
UAL's stock gained $1.125 to $76 a share on the New York Stock Exchange.

It said strong demand for domestic air travel led to a record load factor -- the percent of available seats that are filled by ticketed passengers -- of 69.9 percent, which was up 1.2 points from a year earlier.

The company also set a record in its measurement of revenue per available seat mile, which is a breakdown of income per mile flown by every available seat. UAL said that figure increased by 6.5 percent to 10.2 cents.

Revenue from international travel rose by 6.1 percent, UAL said. Its Latin American unit had strong results, but performance in the Pacific was hurt by currency exchange factors as a result of a weak Japanese yen, the company said.
UAL said it also benefited from labour problems at "one of United's primary competitors."

A contract dispute at American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp., led to a brief pilots strike in February and the surrounding publicity sent passengers scurrying to other airlines to avoid disruptions to their travel plans.
Northwest said it earned $64.6 million, or 58 cents a share, on revenue of $2.38 billion. A year earlier, the airline earned $53.4 million, or 41 cents a share, on revenue of $2.27 billion.
"The year-over-year operating results indicate that the first quarter was challenging and the second quarter looks to be more so," said Jim Lawrence, Northwest executive vice president.

"We are forecasting demand to remain strong in the North American system, but less positively, we don't expect much improvement in fuel prices year-over-year and we expect the yen to continue to be weak.
"Further, capacity in the second quarter will increase less than planned due to the late delivery of five widebody aircraft."
